newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish unions protest public sector wage freeze.
newsitem.headline: Spanish unions protest public sector wage freeze.

text.p: Spanish unions on Monday staged the first in a series of demonstrations against a public sector wage freeze and delivered a protest to parliament to coincide with the official presentation of the 1997 draft budget.

"We hope that from now until December, this government changes its attitude, because if it doesn't the unions will consider stronger pressure methods," said Enrique Alonso of the Confederation of Independent and Public Sector Unions.
He said the wage freeze will cut 1997 forecast growth by 0.7 percent and create 100,000 fewer jobs than expected.
Syndicates are planning a second protest on October 15, after which they will decide whether to call a general strike.
The unions could be heading for a prolonged stand-off with the government, which says the wage freeze -- expected to cut spending by 200 billion pesetas -- is not up for discussion.
